# Pinned WebRTC async driver

Imported library sources from crates.io `webrtc` version 0.21.1, whose packaged
VCS metadata records commit `d658b5a803dd8dc389547450e245877310c9cbed` from
https://github.com/webrtc-rs/webrtc. No upstream submission is made by this fork.

The downloaded crate archive was verified against the registry lock checksum:
`b621e736302bef784948cc8d8099fd0a8fdb5757693c80a344ffbe38c49387d2`.
MIT and Apache licenses are preserved verbatim. This copy includes `src`, the
normalized and original package manifests, README, licenses and VCS metadata. Example and
integration-test target declarations are omitted because those targets are not
vendored. Numeric GitHub issue references in source comments use bare numbers
to comply with this fork's reference policy. Production dependencies and their
version constraints are unchanged. Defaults remain disabled by the parent.

The maintained behavior changes include `peer_connection/driver.rs`:
drain pending TURN writes after draining core writes, before the driver waits
for another event. Core media can enqueue a relay datagram after the earlier
TURN drain; leaving that datagram queued makes an idle final frame wait for an
unrelated network or timer event. Also dispatch core events generated by TURN
decapsulation before draining media, so a remote track exists when its first
RTP packet is delivered. The direct read path already has that ordering.
Direct UDP/GSO behavior is unchanged. The
forced-relay tests in the parent media crate cover actual coturn transport.

`peer_connection/mod.rs` wakes the driver after accepting a remote candidate
when no passive-TCP connect event is enqueued. Candidate insertion can arm an
ICE check deadline or mDNS output while the driver is parked. Without a wake,
late trickle candidates can wait for an unrelated timer/packet. A regression
parks both real-UDP peers after answer processing on held old deadlines, then
allows newly armed ICE timers only after a wake. The same fixture fails without
the wake and passes with it, requiring late candidates to connect and carry
media. An earlier all-timers-blocked fixture failed both versions and is not
used as causal proof; raw results preserve that distinction.
Passive-TCP event ordering is preserved; the existing write wake is coalesced.

Raw socket input additionally pumps core events after each control datagram,
before a following packet in a UDP/GRO or TCP batch. DTLS completion installs
SRTP contexts through that pump; deferring it until after the batch can drop the
first RTP even though ICE/DTLS reaches Connected. The initially configured
one-sided TURN baseline and late-configuration cases fail before this change
and deliver payload afterwards with identical tests. RTP/RTCP retains its
ordinary end-of-burst public-event drain, so steady media does not acquire an
extra immediate pump. The existing core lock is reused, and empty event storage
allocates no vector buffer. This extends handshake ordering independently of
the older track-event-before-media drain on TURN input. Exact source comparisons,
UDP/TCP/TLS allocation oracles and failure logs are retained in the parent's
`results/2026-11-04-late-relay-fallback/` pack. No measured CPU saving is implied.

STUN hostname resolution belongs to the gatherer's discovery phase. Independent
lookup futures are polled without holding the packet driver inside DNS, so local
candidates and direct ICE/DTLS/media progress while a lookup is pending. Resolution
completion wakes the existing coalesced driver channel; creating a STUN client
also schedules its first write there instead of relying on an unrelated packet
or timer. This adds no periodic timer or dedicated OS thread. The phase owns both resolver
futures and STUN clients; completion requires both sets to be empty.

The fork-only `quiesce_stun_gathering_for_restart` method acknowledges a
serialized STUN-only restart boundary through the existing driver FIFO after all
earlier gathering requests. The driver drops the old resolver futures and retires
STUN clients, queued writes/events and old core callbacks before replying. It
retains the ICE/DTLS transports and does not cancel established TURN allocations;
callers with TURN configuration are rejected. The caller must serialize
negotiation and close if cancelled. The media wrapper advances its generation
only after the acknowledgement and still preserves a direct connection observed
there. The former separate interrupt channel is no longer needed because DNS
never holds up the driver's FIFO. The driver's discovery phase is one enum;
no production dependency, steady media listener or dedicated OS thread is added.
The existing Tokio hostname resolver uses its blocking pool; dropping the lookup
future does not promise to interrupt an OS resolver already running there.
Concurrent lookup resource costs are not qualified by the synthetic fixtures.
The earlier pending-DNS, silent-UDP/late-response and actual TURN UDP/TCP/TLS
evidence remains in `results/2026-11-04-stun-startup/` in the parent. That dated
pack describes the preceding interrupt-channel implementation. The causal
direct-video failure/pass, fifteen Linux transport cases, three native macOS
DNS cases and separate ten-case SDK mock scope are retained in
`results/2026-11-04-stun-dns/` in the parent; metadata and resource limits
remain explicit there.

`runtime/mod.rs` adds an optional, default-disabled TURN-only local-address
preference. `transport/turn_relayer.rs` evaluates it once per destination
family using actual bound sockets. The default keeps every interface, and
host/STUN gathering is unchanged. The embedding media wrapper prefers the
OS-selected UDP route only when it is available, otherwise preserving the
caller's explicit alternatives; its TCP/TLS IPC uses one binding per family.
Rebinding reevaluates the preference rather than reusing stale interface IPs.
The two-binding actual-coturn tests require one relay endpoint per peer and
retain both host candidates in automatic mode, followed by nominated media.

`Runtime::turn_gathering_delay` is a default-zero optional policy for incremental
ICE embedders. The existing driver timer schedules deferred TURN, never a sleep
inside the event handler; host/STUN, reads, DTLS, writes and Close remain live.
A Connected event cancels the deferred allocation and completes the TURN part
of gathering. If no connection exists at the deadline, normal TURN gathering
starts. Relay-only mode bypasses the grace; rebind clears stale deferred work.
The wrapper uses 250 ms only for Automatic trickle peers with configured TURN.
Full-SDP callers and the SDK default remain immediate. Actual-coturn fixtures
cover skipped native LAN allocations and delayed UDP/TCP/TLS fallback; a close
fixture requires no late Allocate after its original deadline.

When updating, verify the new package checksum, preserve licenses, reapply this
driver and optional interface changes and rerun the forced UDP/TCP/TLS relay fixtures. URL parsing,
loopback transport tests and native cross-compilation do not replace them.


The fork-only `quiesce_ice_gathering_for_restart` extends the acknowledged
barrier to live TURN discovery. It requires the setting that discards local
candidates and rebinds on restart. The serialized owner stops new media writes;
the driver drains accepted writes while the old relay mapping still exists,
retires discovery/allocations and sends release datagrams before replying.
Only then can the wrapper replace TCP/TLS adapters and advance its generation.
The DTLS object/certificate remain on the same peer. This deliberately obtains
a fresh allocation/socket for a changed username rather than using the imported
relayer's in-place credential-update path: RFC 8656 section 6 requires an
allocation's subsequent requests to keep its original username. The imported
raw SDK credential-only path still needs independent scrutiny; the new media
restart does not depend on it. No dependency version or feature changes.

The media wrapper also retires its old connection/ICE observations after that
acknowledged barrier. A stronger pre-answer readiness regression fails before
this change even though earlier packet-delivery tests passed. Source identities,
the identical before/after test and final UDP/TCP/TLS evidence are retained in
`results/2026-11-05-live-ice-restart/` in the parent media package. This changes
wrapper readiness, not the peer's certificate or RTP timeline.
